Functions of IKKA in cancer cell signalling pathways

Functions of IKKα in cancer cell signalling pathways. Upon DNA damage, IKKα phosphorylates critical components of the DDR pathway, promoting DNA repair. IKKα also regulates the expression of Notch1-target genes. In ERα-signalling, IKKα promotes the estrogen-dependent expression of genes involved in cell cycle progression. IKKα has dual roles in Myc/TGF-β signalling where it promotes the expression of Myc antagonists in SCC, while in prostate cancer it promotes c-Myc transcriptional activity. In Wnt/β-catenin signalling, IKKα prevents the degradation of β-catenin, promoting transcription of its target genes. In mTOR, IKKα enhances mTORC1 activity through phosphorylation, and promotes Akt signalling through association with mTORC2
